observation_summary: The compiler reports an incorrect type name in an error message when a property is missing. Specifically, it reports the name of the object instance (e.g., 'C3.c2_') instead of the type of the object (e.g., 'C2').
hypothesis: The method responsible for generating the readable type name, 'getReadableJSTypeName', performs its logic in the wrong order. It attempts to resolve the qualified name of the node before checking if the type can be resolved to a more meaningful constructor or prototype name, leading to the reporting of the instance name instead of the type name.
prediction: Moving the type resolution logic (dereferencing and checking for constructor/prototype types) to the beginning of the 'getReadableJSTypeName' method will ensure that the correct type name is returned before the method falls back to the qualified name.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the block of code responsible for identifying the type (dereferencing and checking for constructor/prototype) was moved from the end of the method to the beginning. This confirms that the original implementation was incorrectly prioritizing the qualified name over the actual type name.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a procedural error in how the compiler constructs a diagnostic message. The logic for determining the 'readable type name' was ordered such that it fell back to the qualified name (the instance variable) before correctly identifying the underlying type (the constructor). This is a classic algorithmic/procedural ordering issue within a method, fitting the 'Algorithm/Method' ODC type.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows the reordering of logic within 'getReadableJSTypeName'.
The bug report states that the error message reports 'C3.c2_' instead of 'C2'.
The failing test confirms the mismatch in the expected error message string.

The issue is internal to the 'getReadableJSTypeName' method and does not involve a contract mismatch between components.
